news.title: PFF NAMES 14-MAN PMNFT U15 FOR FIFA U15 WORLD CUP & FESTIVAL
news.lede: The Philippine Football Federation (PFF) has named the 14-player squad of the Philippine Under-15 Men’s National Football Team (PMNFT U15) for the inaugural FIFA U15 World Cup & Festival, which will be played in Baku, Azerbaijan, from October 24 to 30, 2026. The tournament uses an 8v8 format. FIFA requires national teams to field 14 players. “Representing the Philippines at the first FIFA U15 World Cup & Festival is a milestone for these young players and for our youth program.

news.title: Lionel Messi: A career in pictures
news.lede: Having started playing football in his native Argentina, Lionel Messi joined Barcelona's youth academy in 2001 at the age of 13. It wasn't long before he was promoted to the first team, making his La Liga debut in October 2004 at the age of 17. The following May he scored his first goal. His first title also came in his debut season, as Barcelona won La Liga in 2004-05.

news.title: Ronaldinho to make football comeback aged 46
news.lede: More than a decade after his last professional appearance, Brazilian superstar Ronaldinho is set for a comeback. The former world player of the year is to play in Italy’s third tier. While Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are still playing at 39 and 41 respectively, most football fans thought Ronaldinho belonged to another footballing era. That all changed in June, when Italian Serie C club, Ravenna, announced that the former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan forward would play for them in the upcoming season.

news.title: Zambia thrash Portugal to win FIFA U-15 World Cup Tier B title
news.lede: Zambia’s Under-15 national team produced an impressive performance to beat Portugal 5-2 and clinch the Tier B title at the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan. Maxen Msimuko led the charge with a hat-trick, while Benson and Thomson also found the net as the Junior Chipolopolo capped their campaign with a convincing victory over their European opponents. Samuel Musonda also came close to getting on the scoresheet, striking the crossbar as Zambia dominated the contest to secure the title. The triumph marks a significant achievement for the young Zambian side, who competed against teams from across the world at the landmark youth football festival.

news.title: New Zealand finish FIFA U-15 Boys’ World Cup with finals victory over Ethiopia
news.lede: New Zealand have finished the inaugural FIFA U-15 Boys’ World Cup in Azerbaijan with a 2-1 victory against Ethiopia in their Tier F final. The win at Baku’s Crystal Hall completed a successful turnaround for the New Zealanders, who lost four of their five qualification matches. They recovered to win their next four games, including a penalty shootout victory over Nepal in their semi-final.
